text_fidelity_a:
SHUBHADA Folding Pocket Knives Multi Function Emergency Tool Knives Led Light Magnesium fire starter Seatbelt cutter Glass breaker Bottle opener（Colorful Titanium） What I like about this knife:
It's a sharp looking knife with a cool multi-functional design. The blade opens well and I can easily release the lock to close it. The blade is strong, sharp and durable. It clips to my jeans and stays there because the clip is tight so I can either use the sheath to carry it or just clip to jeans without the sheath. The little LED light is pretty bright.

What I don't like about this knife:
Although the LED light is bright, I'm not too crazy about how it functions. It's easy enough to understand turning the light tighter to turn it on and loosening to turn it off. But on the knife I received you really have to remove the light from it's magnetic hold area on the knife in order to turn the knife on and use it. It would have been nice to be able to screw the LED tighter while in the knife since that would make it much easier in an emergency, and there would be less risk of dropping or losing the little flashlight. Maybe the intention with this design was to be able to keep the light affixed while using it, but mine just doesn't work that way. So there is that.

Overall it's a great knife and I like it a lot! It's priced reasonably, functions well, looks sharp, and it would also make a nice gift.
text_fidelity_b: SHUBHADA Folding Pocket Knives Multi Function Emergency Tool Knives Led Light Magnesium fire starter Seatbelt cutter Glass breaker Bottle opener（Colorful Titanium）

text_fidelity_a:
Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote This is a comfortable back pack.
The selling point for me was that it was listed to be able to accept an additional water bladder. And for me, (I hike in the Phoenix, AZ area mountains during the midday summer heat) that is important. Two 3liter bladders are a standard for me. Normally, I have to move up to my 35 litter backpack during the summer because the straps on my other packs are too narrow to adequately support the weight of two 3liter bladders (6 kilos or about 13lbs) in addition to my emergency first aid supplies, food, phone, and anything else I have. In total, about 25lbs (a little more than 11 kilos).

So it was a pleasant surprise that the straps on this 20 liter pack were almost as wide as the straps on my 35 liter pack. Making this pack easily able to comfortably carry the weight.

Also the waist belt has molle webbing for attaching additional things. For me, that's a phone carrier on one side and a 4x6 pouch on the other for some trail snacks (if I need the nourishment on the trail). A big plus. I don't have to remove the backpack to have a snack or to put the empty wrapper back in the pouch.
The waist belt also helps keep everything stable when I am trail running (probably about half of my normal 10 mile hike is trail running)

The padding on this backpack is much better than any of my other backpacks regardless of size. (I have 3l,6l,12l,18l,20l,25l,30l, and 35l backpacks.) Yes, I have a lot because I've never been able to find a nearly perfect fit for my needs, until now.

The bladder - this is a high quality bladder. (I now have four of them.) It has a nice high water flow. I'm easily drinking more during my hike because of this high flow rate. With my other bladders, I averaged about 1 liter an hour consumption. With these bladders, I average 1.5 liters an hour consumption. I have my garmin watch set to give a reminder every 8 minutes to drink water. So with the old bladders and the new Source bladders, I was drinking at the same intervals, it's just easier to drink through the Source drinking tube than the other ones resulting in the higher consumption.

Strap management - this thing has elastic on each of the straps to hold the excess strapping. Wow, so nice. No Irish pennants (marine corps terminology referring to the the stray threads sticking out on clothing) flying all over the place

I do have one complaint though, it says that it'll accept a second bladder. But there's only the one strap in the water bladder compartment to hold a bladder. To accommodate a second bladder, you have to place it in the main storage compartment. But there is no strap to hold a bladder there. And you have farther to run the tube for this second bladder. I started keeping some storage at the bottom of the main compartment (sun block, towels, etc.) that manages to raise up the second bladder so that the drinking tube for that bladder isn't uncomfortably short to drink through. Otherwise the second bladder sits low enough that the tube is a little short (perhaps about 5 or 6 inches shorter than the tube for the water bladder in the water bladder compartment).
text_fidelity_b: Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote

text_fidelity_a:
AIM Sports Shotgun Shell Bandolier/56 Rounds I own two of these now. Both are fully loaded, one with slugs and the other with OO buck. If something bad happens and I have to react quickly, I can criss-cross the two bandoliers, grab my Remington Mariner, and have two different loads at my fingertips immediately. A total of 112 rounds should give me plenty of firepower to handle most problems without worrying about using up my ammo.

Using two at a time makes sense for two reasons. One is that you know which load is in which bandolier. The other is that the opposing weight of having one over each shoulder helps keep you in balance when shooting. Good shooting is all about balance and confidence.

On the other hand, maybe I should switch to a high capacity .22 long rifle. I could carry a lot more ammo with far less weight. But nothing generates the immediate respect of the sound of a shotgun being racked. Might as well let them know that something serious is on the way. Chances are they'll bug out before they have the pleasure of meeting you.
text_fidelity_b: AIM Sports Shotgun Shell Bandolier/56 Rounds

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings. The foot warmer seems to be made of good quality fabric and leather.

The foot warmer has three temperature settings: 38C (100F), 42C (108F), and 55C (131F). When I turned the foot warmer on at room temperature, it listed 22C. I adjusted the temperature to the hottest setting of 55C. I kept it going for 45 minutes, with both my feet in the warmer. After 20 minutes or so the warmer stabilized at a temperature of 43 to 44C. 25 minutes later, the temperature had not changed, never reaching anywhere close to 55C. 44C was warm enough, but not what was promised.

Besides the temperature limit, two drawbacks for me (may not apply to other people):
- The foot warmer has USB-C input, and it comes with a USB-A to USB-C cable. Note that the warmer only accepts 10W, and if you try to use a USB-C to USB-C cable that delivers higher wattage, the foot warmer will not work. Ideally the foot warmer's electronics would be designed to take as much wattage as they need, and no more, in the same way I can connect an iphone and an ipad pro to the same fast-charging brick, and each device would accept only as much wattage as appropriate, instead of burning out or shutting down.
- This foot warmer seems to be designed for those who shoe sizes 11 and under. I wear size 13 shoes, and my feet barely fit, with my toes partially curled. Pretty uncomfortable. The product description makes no reference to foot size, and unfortunately for me, I cannot use this foot warmer effectively. Otherwise, it does its job well.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings.

text_fidelity_a: Abus Bordo 5700 Folding Lock This is a very nifty bike lock. It comes with a sheath that you can Velcro onto the frame of your bike. When the lock is not in use then you store it in the sheath, and it is very easy to take out the lock when you need to secure your bike. The only thing I am concerned about is if the lock will not stay inside the sheath after it gets older and time passes. It comes with two keys, but it would be really nice if they included a third key. That way you could keep one on your keychain, store one at home, and store one at work or wherever you ride and park the most. The entire lock is covered with a plastic or silicone type material so when it hits your bike it will prevent it from denting or chipping the paint. It will take some time to get used to the way it opens and unfolds if you are used to a loose rope chain type lock. The storage aspect of this is strong, the bag will certainly hold up, and it will hold a good amount of stuff. It's also quite easy to install on any bike, and it will fit every standard sized cell phone.

The phone holding aspect might need a little work. Yes, it does work, and you can access your screen buttons through the plastic. If you're using this for an "always on" function - like Maps or Youtube Music - then you'll think it's just fine. If you want any acces to your power and volume buttons, or your headphone jack, or if you plan on listening to a podcast or music that doesn't require your screen to be on, then you'll need to stop in order to adjust or turn on your screen, as these functions will be hidden underneath a stiff zipper and a velcro pad.

There are other phone holding devices you can clip on your bike that will allow you full access to everything, and if this is what you need, then you should buy those products instead of this one. If you want a deep storage compartment for bike tools or other items, and want "always on" functionality, then this is a great buy.

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Little Jumpers Trampoline 786 I do not recommend the Alex Little Jumper Trampoline unless space is an issue. For $23 less you can purchase the significantly larger and more stable [[ASIN:B008BIV87M Bazoongi 48" Trampoline Bouncer with Easy Hold Handle Bar - Sunshine Yellow. Special Exclusive Limited Edition]].

The instructions are worthless. For example, one part states to "attach the bungee cord to the cord lock by pulling the knotted end of the cord tight". Can I just start by saying "What?" Well there is no knotted end, so you have to create it, though it doesn't really tell you how to do that. Then you have the issue of only three helpful images for the entire manual. And I probably need to start by saying I like to consider myself rather capable when it comes to assembling items and frames of structures having helped my father build our homes and additions. The instructions also do not elaborate where the knotted end should go in reference to the trampoline itself. You can figure out where it needs to go in the medal cord lock, but not on the trampoline itself. The only picture shows half of the trampoline having the cord wrapped around it so you are left wondering what the starting point looks like.

I hazarded a guess and just went with it at that point. Once I wrapped everything around and made sure that I pulled the cord tight several times I then tied it off. The instructions are then once again really vague; therefore I knotted the last end of the cord by itself and pulled it through the medal fastener. I then proceeded to knot the last end of the cord that I had just wrapped around with the beginning part of the cord to ensure an additional sense of security. The instructions mention nothing of this but after looking at the final results, with pieces of cord jutting out in random places, I knew that my three youngest would see that as an invitation to mess with it. So I knotted both ends together, and I did that twice. My kids can be rather problematic.

The directions then tell you to place the cover on the trampoline, making sure that it fits. Once again, the instructions lack on details. They do not specify that the cover should be placed in a specific direction. I used the writing on the cover as an indication for direction, placing the writing outwards where the handle will go. Otherwise, the cover does not fit. I found this out through trial and error, of course. There are also plastic clips that apparently must be clipped to the trampoline in some fashion, that you obviously have to figure out on your own. The most obvious thing was to clip them to the bungee cords that were wrapped around the trampoline.

The next step is to secure the handle. And yet again, those wonderful directions prove that they are pointless. I finally just put the small yellow bar into the curved handle portion (not attaching to the trampoline base yet) to get a sense of where it should go in the actual trampoline frame. I was then able to figure out which direction it faced, knowing that screws would be added at the end. REALLY not clear, but I was able to figure out having put together dozens of pieces before.

All in all, given that it was purchased at a discounted price, it will work out fine in addition to our other in home trampoline. This might be alright for one child, but it would definitely not work for my three kids (4 yr old twins and a 2 yr old) if I did not have the second larger trampoline. They are the ultimate test in terms of durability for any toy and this one is unfortunately not built for heavy duty usage. This might be fine on its own for occasional use from a calmer child, which none of mine are.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Little Jumpers Trampoline 786

Rule number two of lightweight bicycle components is everything must be installed with a torque wrench. If you read stories of Thomson components failing soon after purchase, the bolts have been torqued too much.

Seatpost looks sleek, though the setback version is an acquired taste. The adjustability is excellent and the side markers allow you to set your seat angle with a great deal of precision. I'll probably buy another one.

The straps and my hands got along well. I hated the ones in the community because they were thin, no comfort, and made lifting any sort of weight deeply uncomfortable; so much so I stopped even trying. But as for the lifting in the gym, it is giving me exactly what I want and I’ve instantly felt my game go up. Very pleased. text_fidelity_a:
SUUNTO Movestick Mini (Black, One Size) worked with my Garmin 310XT on my Mac Pro without having to install anything. I already had the Garmin ANT+ stick installed and was using that, I simply took that out of the USB slot and put this in. I though I'd have to install something but after awhile the Garmin started syncing to it. Love that it worked right away. Although some times after a workout it takes a bit longer for it to recognize and connect automatically to my Garmin 310xt and start the data transfer. Usually I just leave the ANT+ stick in my Mac and synch my workouts after I'm done. However on a recent out of town trip I had forgotten to pack the ANT+ stick so I needed a replacement. I had read that this works just as well as the Garmin (some reviewers say even better) so at a significantly lower price and smaller size than the Garmin stick, I decided to give this a try so that I could keep it with my MacBook Pro that I use when traveling. I am very pleased with it and it is definitely worth it for the better price and works just as well as the Garmin stick, except for the occasional times when it doesn't seem to find the Garmin. When that happens I've just pulled it out and put it back in the USB slot and it usually finds the Garmin and starts transferring the data.

In Summary:

Pros:
+ Works great with Mac OSX - just plug it in!
+ cheaper than the Garmin ANT+ stick
+ small form factor - so no worry about accidentally bumping it against it and knocking it out of the USB slot during data transfer

Cons:
+ Some times takes a while to recognize my Garmin 310xt
+ small form factor - could get lost easily - but this is not really an issue to me, though may be for some folks so thought I'd mention it.

Conclusion: If it didnt' have that occasional little blip of not connecting, I'd give it 5 stars. Still I'm very pleased with it and would definitely recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: SUUNTO Movestick Mini (Black, One Size)

Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue) A bit of a conumdrum here with two ways to look at it. I am 6'3" and currently weigh 225 Lbs. Not a lightweight but as my Pulmonologist informs me "you're no longer clinically obese, you're just obese". Thanks Doc! A left-handed compliment if I ever heard one.

And there lies the rub. The first time I shook this out I had mild difficulty in getting the tabs and latches to hook up-- like I did just now. That seems to inspire a little less confidence in how safely it will support me without crashing down. Once it is expanded and set up it appears to be pretty sturdy. The color also makes it easy to see in the yard.

But having just had double knee replacement I was a bit concerned that it would hold me without making me faceplant in the yard. When I asked my wife to watch me sit on it in the kitchen she said "don't do that!". The sight of me pulling it out and clicking it together didn't inspire confidence in her either.

It did hold me while sitting still although I was a bit reluctant to shift my weight around on it. That would be my major sticking point. On a yard that is not completely level I know that I would have to be careful. The other part of that is that leaning forward or to one side suddenly puts additional stress on whichever part of the base is sitting on the ground. I am not convinced that leaning over wouldn't cause the stool to buckle and me to fall over.

So there it is. It seems to be a smart design and should solve the problem of having a stool available when needed. However plastic is not indestructible and will often bend as it is stressed over and over again. Good idea, decent execution, but it doesn't inspire any confidence for someone my size.
text_fidelity_b: Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue)

text_fidelity_a: microSHIFT Right Bar End Shifter 11-Speed Mountain for Shimano DynaSys It does what it’s supposed to but it’s not without issues. The friction mode does not have any sort of ratcheting like some nicer lever do. This just makes it a little easier to move the lever and tell how far you’ve moved it when you shift quickly. It works fine but it would have been nice to have a smoother actuation in friction mode. In indexed mode, the lack of smoothness when shifting is less of a problem as you have the index points to overcome anyway and there’s enough resistance at each index position that you’ll rarely shift past your intended gear on accident. The lever does have quite a bit of play it it, however. It would have been nice to have seen tighter tolerance in the index positions. I have enough slop in mine after just a year of use that I can partially disengage a gear without bumping past the index notch. Not a huge deal, and sometimes its actually nice to have that wiggle room, but it would be better in my opinion if the indexing was more precise. If I wanted to finesse it in to gear, I’d use it in friction mode…

So yes, we have two different ones. That said, I was jumping one day and got the rope caught on something on the sidewalk, it hung up enough it caught my foot and almost took me out. Additionally, living in Florida, we can go through times of rain and limits out ability to do outside workouts. Jump ropes are not conducive to indoor homes.

I started to see these no-rope jump ropes and finally paid attention. This one caught my eye and I’m glad it did.

It eliminates that fear or actual act of getting hung up and catching you. I am already feeling much better about jumping with the no-rope. Secondly, we have only done it inside. That means we have another place to jump, and in Florida (hot, humid) or up north (cold, snow) one can jump rope all year round.

The system is great: it counts accurately how much you do. Plus can keep track of weight, time jumping, and repositions. It’s great. I do have 50-something eyes, so I have my wife turn it on/off - buttons are a little hard and I’m not wearing my readers - but otherwise it’s 100% on point for a product. Would say the handles feel at once a little cheap, as far as the read out - but also like they’ll last and take the punishment. It’s strange, but we have confidence in them.

Overall we are very happy with this idea and this product and happy to recommend.

Nite Ize GLC12-31-R3 Gear Clippable Reusable Rubber Twist Tie, 12-inch, 1 Pack, Bright Orange Okay, this thing is flat-out handy! Whoever came up with this must have done a lot of camping. You've been there, yes? When you're trying to find something in your tent at night and you bump your head on the lantern that is hanging from a flimsy fabric scrap sewn into the top of your tent with a single piece of thread (with love from China) and the simple swinging action of your micro LED lantern releases the tab and sends it plummeting into the plushy depths of your sleeping bag where the brilliant glow is muted to nothing RIGHT when you really needed to see if you were putting your underwear on backwards. Or - even more fun - when you've rented a screened shelter at a state park for the night and you realize there is not a single dang nail to be found from which you could hang your light so you have a set it down, pick it up, set it down, pick it up then shove it in your mouth kind-of a problem solving experience.

Ah, Nite Ize. How did you know?!! Now I can hang my lantern just about anywhere I want. I can even bend it around a small tree branch and clip it up high while I scrub the dishes with about a thousand spiders in the dark. I can also quickly loop the gear tie holding the micro lantern around my son's neck so he doesn't drop his flashlight in the magical blue pit of the campground Port-a-Potty. (*Splash* MOM!!!) And - probably the most valuable use - I can clip frequently used items from your neon yellow self and hang you in a really obvious place so I don't have to be asked {repeatedly} where the grill lighter/roasting stick/marshmallow bag/trash bucket is. And at night, when I remove the lantern and let you hold my spider spray, I know you've got my back. Thanks, Nite Ize, for making camping a little bit easier!
text_fidelity_b: Nite Ize GLC12-31-R3 Gear Clippable Reusable Rubber Twist Tie, 12-inch, 1 Pack, Bright Orange

Trail Camera 4k 32MP, Wildlife Camera 120°Monitoring Fast 0.2s Trigger Speed, Hunting Game Cameras Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof IP66 for Outdoor, 940nm No Glow, 32GB SD Card Included [[VIDEOID:4e0b9184b5c9003d3a336d7a4e1f708a]] UPDATE: Below I said I might add corn pictures. Well, I did. I set the camera up on my garden 80 days or so ago from the time of this writing not knowing what I'd get or if I'd get. I learned that the cam saves a video each day averaging around 400 megs. 75 videos and I was out of space, just 4 or 5 days before I was going to take the cam down anyway. I just uploaded my two months in two minutes thirty video. I had the cam set to snap a few frames every 10 minutes. If I had it to over again I would have gone for a half hour. Mebbe and hour between runs. You can judge for yourself. This is a heck of a cam for the dough! Thanks, whoever made this thing. Ya done good!

Let's get the one thing I don't like out of the way. The micro SD card. But, looks like all the cams are going to them so it is what it is. Just be darn careful when removing in the woods. I immediately stash mine in one of those full size adapter sleeves before I put them into a sandwich bag to bring home.

The GREAT part. I have a couple of late model trail cams plus a couple of vintage Tascos. I can tell you with no fear of contradiction my new Trail Camera 4K 32MP, Wildlife Camera has the best video definition of all of them. I was astounded, really. Then, the ad blurb promises that the little SD card is included. Well, I've heard that one before so I wasn't surprised when it wasn't in the box. But I was fooled. It was already in the camera! That was a bonus! Another unexpected bonus was the well written instruction booklet in perfect English, not engrish.

Listen, when you open the case for the first time you'll appreciate that it's a pro camera. The design is pretty much like all of them as for controls but the unit looks and feels more deluxe. It's got a newer spiffier look to it. The software in my other two late models is pretty much the same. The setup screen in my Trail Camera 4K 32MP, Wildlife Camera is different, and better, newer.

I haven't had a chance to move it to the woods yet so for the test I attached it to a pecan tree about 30 yards behind the house. The house takes up nearly all of the frame. Well, out of the box as for sensitivity it defaults to medium. Comes in low to high. Well, set on medium the thing took photos about every two minutes. I finally noticed that every time a car would come by it would snap. The road is at least 100 feet away from the camera and one side of the frame you can't even see it. (The side motion sensors can see it though.) Insane sensitivity. I set it down to low and it's perfect. Got great sound too and the time/temp etc readout at the bottom is excellent.

I could go on but I see most others are reporting out great results as well. For your money you can't do better. I highly recommend this trail cam!
PS.... I intend to stash this thing in my garden this spring to use it for time lapse. Mebbe I'll post my corn coming up this summer! A grand bonus with this cam! This is the one you have been looking for, and PS, remember for my first test it kept popping movies until I adjusted the sensitivity? It filled up the 32G card in about 4 days. NO noticeable drain of the batteries. I'm confident this thing will last a long time posted on a lonely tree. Big time!

And PS... Of great importance. How many times have you seen your photo subject look into the camera of an evening with what you're using now? As someone else noted at night there are no lights. Zip. Nada. True infrared. No sound from the unit either. Super stealth!
text_fidelity_b: Trail Camera 4k 32MP, Wildlife Camera 120°Monitoring Fast 0.2s Trigger Speed, Hunting Game Cameras Night Vision Motion Activated Waterproof IP66 for Outdoor, 940nm No Glow, 32GB SD Card Included

Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain First off, these are by far the brightest reflective anything I've ever bought, and I've bought >20 wrist bands, arm bands, leg bands, vests, .... Photons apparently hate this material: every single photon that hits it immediately turns right around and heads back where it came from. You will be seen when you're wearing these. They're so bright you may be seen from space. :)

Second, customer service can't be beat. I ordered both the the wrist bands and the leg bands, but only received the wrist bands. I contacted the vendor, Mark, and he sent the leg bands out within 12 hours of receiving my email. Later I had a problem with the reflective material separating from the neoprene on one one of the wrist bands, and Mark didn't just replace the one that failed, he sent me a whole new pair, and very quickly. So this is a low-risk purchase: if you have any issues, Mark will make it right for you.

One thing I'm not fond of is that the hook portion of the hook and loop closure is too long. Unless the band fits perfectly around your leg, a good sized section of the hook portion will be exposed, and can snag on cyclists' lycra gear. I wish the hook portion was just an inch long. The 3" loop portion would still allow a couple of inches of flexibility re length.

Also, I'm not sure why these have both extra long hook and loop closures and are made of stretchy neoprene. Both seem intended to allow the band to fit different diameters of legs + clothing, so I'm not sure why you need both. And the stretchy neoprene makes it much more likely that the relatively delicate reflective material will separate from it, as happened with 1 of the 4 bands I originally purchased. I'd prefer the fabric to not stretch to minimize the risk of failure, and just use the velcro to adjust the length. But since Mark backs up the product if it fails, this is a small deal.

Overall, I'm happy with these. I believe they're the brightest reflective bands you can buy, so if you want to be seen, these will do the job.
text_fidelity_b: Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain

text_fidelity_a:
SKLZ Professional Grade Strength Training Resistance Band (40-Inch) Now, who wouldn't love owning a giant rubber band? :D I'm mildly allergic to synthetic latex, but I'm fine with natural latex. This resistance band is made with natural rubber latex, and I've had no allergic reaction to it. I've only used it for a few days now, and a certain latex smell does rub off onto my hands and skin from use, but I'm assuming this will disappear with use. The band is 0.5" wide, 0.25" thick, and about 40" in length (or a 84" outer circumference).

The band comes with a booklet with arm and leg strength-building exercises. Ten use just the band and your body. Nine require a door anchor (not included) along with the band. The product video--available online--briefly shows ways to use the band to improve speed or to assist exercises. The box says it can be used to improve flexibility, but I haven't seen any suggested exercises for the band with that focus.

I like resistance bands, but most are uncomfortable to stand on or difficult to grip. My right hand is weak, so doing strength exercises with bands that require a strong grip aren't very useful to me. This band looked like something I could get my whole body into (somewhat literally) so I thought I could modify the exercises so my weak grip wouldn't matter. Well, most of their suggested exercises do have you gripping the band with your hands, but other suggested exercises do work well for me. I had no problem standing on the band--it's squared rather than round and 0.25" thick. The band appears to be well-made and likely to last well.

I'm a 5'4" woman and I live on a farm, so I regularly lift 25-50lbs. If I bought a resistance band, I'd probably go with the Low rather than Medium, at least to start out. I could do the leg exercises with the Medium band, but most of the arm strength exercises were very difficult (partly due to my weak hand). My dad--nearly 6' tall and still strong at 68 years old--could do both leg and arm exercises and get a good workout from them. He even modified some exercises to do while sitting down as he's wanted some exercises he can do while watching TV. I do wish they had more suggested exercises than the arm and leg strengthening ones, but I'm sure I can modify some traditional exercises.

There is a limited, 1 year warranty. It's made in Thailand.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Professional Grade Strength Training Resistance Band (40-Inch)

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included) I have been using a cheap basic tracker for over a year.  I liked how it worked for the most part but accuracy was way off (workouts would undercount steps but I could ride the mower for 45 mins and get 2 days worth of steps).  My wife talked me into upgrading to an actual fitbit.  After reading reviews and product descriptions and pouring over videos I had narrowed it down to the charge 4, the charge 3, and a Samsung offering.  Well the price tag on the Samsung put it out, and the charge 3 is selling for as much as a 4.  After a very frustrating wait on a prime shipment (7 days when it should have been 2) the watch arrived.  First and foremost there are NO directions so forget about learning any of the features by reading (whatever).  The app is somewhat complicated and very difficult to figure out.  After several hours of frustrating and useless attempts I finally have up and packed it all up to be sent back (mind you my battery went from 72% to 14%).  The next day I wore the watch to spite myself and it did record my steps accurately.  I played with it more that night and got some of the features to work but I still could not get my texts.  My daughter took over and figured out what I was doing wrong (had the do not disturb turned on at the watch- but not in the app) which brings me to my next huge issue.  Some of the features can only be accessed from the watch, some only from the app, and some from either.  SO frustrating.  So after getting everything FINALLY set up I wore the watch all day and night.  Everything worked and I got a sleep score and all was good.  3 days later and some of the features have stopped working.  Sleep score no longer records (but it tells me how much I sleep and all the jazz).  Workout target zone does not work now (I must have turned off something that records this info).  I can't seem to answer my texts thru the watch at all.  To activate the screen is a practice of futility.  Some times 2 or 3 taps will turn on the screen and sometimes I have to tap the screen 50 to 100 times, and sometimes the only way to activate the screen is with the button (I do have a cover on mine but still).  There are some really nice things about the watch.  Switch bands is a breeze and takes less than a minute, and the bands hold well.  Most texts are easy to read and I have not run out of space on longer texts (my last watch was limited to 2 screens and 2 words).  Battery life has been excellent (4 days of messing around with settings and what not and still at 48%).  Bluetooth range is amazing (15 feet in a lot of cases).  Step count is super accurate (often within 20 steps of my wife's watch when we do workouts together).  There are some cool faces and apps you can add to the watch.  Overall I'm feeling pretty neutral on Fitbit in general.  There is a lot of info provided but the app is so unfriendly and hard to figure out.  There is to much fiddling around between the watch and the app as to be frustrating.  Even the "How to Use" section on the app is worthless (it tells you features, but not how to turn them on or off).  I am keeping the watch because it does track what I want, but would not recommend it to anyone new to tracker apps as trying to learn this app is way to complicated.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a: MICLON Cybertrack 100 Electric Bike for Adults, 2X Faster Charge, 350W BAFANG Motor, 36V 10.4AH Removable Battery, 20MPH 26'' Mountain Ebike, Shimano 21 Speed, Suspension Fork, LED Display I'm a 75 year old man who has been riding a regular bike for years and years but my knees were telling me that hills were no longer their friend. I moved from a place with NO hills to a place where hills are everywhere so I decided to look in to an ebike that was within my budget. This bike seemed to be just what I needed so I decided to give it a shot...First thing was it was very easy to assemble (Youtube helped)..then I decided to take it for a spin. This bike is a completely different experience so my advise would be to practice in a place that's deserted...so here's the low down on my first week of riding on a regular basis....first, this bike will get up and go and reach 20 mph very fast, and for me that was my first surprise, then getting a feel for the 5 levels of resistance 1 being the most and 5 is where you hardly pedal at all, but here's where you need to pay attention....the throttle takes up about half the right handle bar so it's very easy to accelerate when you don't want to so pay attention...then there the issue with the kick stand which seems be very wobblily and a little unstable....having said that, I really like this bike, it's very easy and fun when you get used to it...quick note, I would not leave my house with charger plugged it just to be safe...So now on July 13th or having the bike for over a month the only thing that is driving me nuts is the kick stand...it flops down over and over again even after tightening the so called locking mechanism..it is aggravating and turns my bike ride into a hassle.....it's a terrible TERRIBLE design....................*******.........So I've  owned the bike almost 4 months and I continue to love this bike, I replaced the kick stand and replaced the seat with one a lot more comfortable, The one thing that, for me, makes the ride safer and more predictable is....if I'm riding near people or on roads with intersections I keep the resistance on 1 or 0 and use the hand throttle to provide power to the bike. I used to keep it on 2-4 but found that when I wanted to stop if any pressure was put on the pedals when trying to stop immediately throws the bike forward when you're not expecting it..I learned the hard way and it wasn't pretty..In my opinion controlling the bike with the hand throttle is the safest except if your riding on a trail or on a road with no stop and go...This in my opinion is the best and safest way to operate the bike with the electric assist....aside from that this is a great entry level bike at a very good price.  I look forward to many more miles of fun...
text_fidelity_b: MICLON Cybertrack 100 Electric Bike for Adults, 2X Faster Charge, 350W BAFANG Motor, 36V 10.4AH Removable Battery, 20MPH 26'' Mountain Ebike, Shimano 21 Speed, Suspension Fork, LED Display

PROS:
1) The low profile pocket clip doesn't scratch the crap out of my car paint as my kershaw did.
2) The metal is not as good as my kershaw, but it is VERY VERY close.
3) A ceramic hone works best after sharpening.
4) You can get this thing RAZOR sharp, but it dulls after a moderate amount of use.
5) It is SUPER light, and very fast.
6) Initially the opening mechanism is weird getting used to. However once you do, it is actually very easy to use.
7) The short blade does NOT impede its performance as I originally thought. You can think the belly of the knife for this, it adds a nice additional cutting surface.
8) The anodized aluminum is fairly slip resistant.
9) The thumb studs protrude enough for you to get a good open on it.
10) It is very sleek looking and the POP is an attention getter.
11) It is pretty ergonomic and it fits in the hand pretty well.

CONS:
1) It is difficult getting adjusted to the opening mechanism.
2) The "safety" makes me feel like this thing will jump open in my pocket if I don't have it turned on.... even though it probably wont.
3) I don't care for lock back knives as it impedes one handed use. I now can use it one handed though which took some practice.
4) The metal is odd, things you think would dull it won't.... but the things you don't think would will.. I.E. it cuts through weed eater string like a beast but a couple pieces of thin cardboard has this blade spent.
5) Tape and other adhesives stick to this blade BAD... My kershaw had a Teflon coating. Something I wished this one had.
6) the top of the pocket clip sticks up about 3/16 of an inch from the knife.... it is just odd to me. It doesn't really affect the functionality however.

Even though I questioned my purchase at first, I am very happy with my purchase. For this price you get a PERFECT edc knife. Just make sure that you have at least an 800-1200 grit diamond stone and a ceramic hone for quick sharpening.

text_fidelity_a:
Bowflex SelectTech 552 Adjustable Dumbbells It's hard to beat the convenience of going to a rack and picking up a couple of steel dumbbells of fixed weight, and relatively compact size, but who wants to spend $1,500-$3000, not to mention the environmental waste of producing 800+ pounds of steel for a single person's home gym?

I purchased this set of multi-weight dumbbells for my home gym that I use 4 times a week. I've only had them for a couple of weeks so I can't speak to their longevity, but I DO believe these are an excellent alternative to a full set of gym weights, if you accept the small compromises that come with this type of device. Many of the criticisms I see in other reviews seem to focus on these compromises so I enumerate them here, as well as some advantages, for the potential buyer.

This set offers balanced dumbbell weights from 5 to 25 pounds in 2.5lb increments, and from 25-55 in 5 pound increments. One of the advantages of these weights is the ability to adjust each end of the dumbbell independently. From 5 to 25 pounds, each SIDE increases by 1.25 pounds. It is thereore possible to set a weight of 6.25 or 8.75 pounds per dumbbell, understanding that there is a 1.25 pound difference from one end to the other-not a big deal-especially at lower weights. From 25 to 55 pounds you can similarly increase weights by just 2.5 pounds to give even more weight options. I find this a big plus.

The entire set weighs just 110 pounds and takes up very little space. You COULD spend the $150 on the dedicated rack, or, if you have basic woodworking tools, for about $50 you can buy a 4' x 8' x 3/4 sheet of plywood and a box of 2" construction screws and build simple boxes to hold the weights. (see picture)

Compromises:
1. The length of each dumbbell is longer than a standard dumbbell. For many excersises that doesn't matter, but for some you have to make some adjustments to how you perform the motions-it's the trade off for the convenience of being able to dial in the weight you want on a single bar.

2. You have to learn to remove and replace the weights straight and vertically out of the cradles. Once you get the hang of it, it's not a big deal.

3. If you are using identical weights on each side of the dumbbells, you can replace them into the cradles without regard to which side is which. However, if you do want to set the two sides at different weights, you will have to replace them the right way into the cradles. It's not rocket science, but it's something you have to be aware of and get used to.

4. The design allows for a small amount of play between the weight plates and the barbell they are attached to. So they can rattle a little. It's not like they are going to fall apart, but it isn't a solid unit like a dedicated dumbbell....you get use to it.

Those are my thoughts on this multiweight set. For a few extra seconds of set up for each weight, and proper handling during removal and replacement to the trays, you get a full range set of dumbbells at a fraction of the cost, and weight, and space requirement of a full rack set.
text_fidelity_b: Bowflex SelectTech 552 Adjustable Dumbbells

text_fidelity_a:
Everlast Reflex Bag (EA) [[VIDEOID:36c82b800aaf42202e179eeb3c1739a5]] I got this bag for my 9 year old son because he has some coordination issues. I wanted him to work eye hand coordination and get some exercise. He really enjoys working out with this reflex bag.

We filled our base with a 50 lb bag of sand rather than water. I figured that it would end up in the house and I didn't like the idea a flood on wood floors if it leaked. Also that quanity of sand is twice as heavy as the same amount of water. This means the bag will stay upright if it gets hit hard. The play sand that we used had to be dried on a tarp to get it to pour into the opening. When it was damp it had to be forced into the opening and it took a long time to get a small quantity of sand inside. Other than that it was very easy to assemble. Everlast provides a hex key and a cheap stamped out wrench to assemble the bag.

It does unscrew slightly form the base as it is struck. This should not be a deal breaker for you, but something you need to be aware of.

Other reviewers have posted negative reviews must be hitting this bag with powerful blows. From my experience a reflex bag is more for speed and reflex training than power blows. If you want to lay into something with power, get a heavy bag. It will suit you much better.

For our use we are very happy with the bag. I think any kid would really enjoy this as a gift. Dad likes it too, and I like that my son getting some exercise rather than sitting in his room playing with his Nintendo DSi.

We got the Everlast 8 ounce Youth gloves to go with this Reflex Bag. I would recommend them as they offer good wrist support and excellent construction.

[[ASIN:B000QSQKDW Everlast Pro Style 8-Ounce Youth Training Gloves]]

Update5/26/10: Yesterday one on my son's friend used a bat on the reflex bag. It is not bat proof. It knocked the bag off. I poured Gorilla glue into the hole and on the post and let it dry with the post pointed up for a day. It seems as good as new.

Update 7/3/10 The bag is better than new. Two kids parties and near daily use and the bag is still firmly on the pole. The Gorilla glue has secured this bag with no sign of wiggle. They should manufactur them like this.

Update 11/8/11 The bag is still on as good as when I first glued it. No wiggle. The unit has been stored on our patio and is starting to rust at the spring and shaft. Nothing that affects the performance. It's just not that sightly. My son wants a B.O.B. Body Opponent Bag It is a training bag that looks like a torso. $250...ouch.
text_fidelity_b: Everlast Reflex Bag (EA)

text_fidelity_a:
Grizzly Gear Emergency Survival Mylar Thermal 2 Person Sleeping Bag - Accommodates 2 Adults - 64" X 87" As you know, the point of these emergency blankets is to use them when everything else has failed. You are not at home (or the power and gas is out), you can't get to relatives, a hotel, or a Red Cross shelter... Or perhaps you are literally lost in the woods and thanking your lucky stars you threw an emergency blanket in your daypack..

The only difference here is that two people can fit, and if you have ever had to worry about hyperthermia, you know that the body heat of another is about the only way to bring up the body heat of the severely chilled person.

On a trail crew as an older teen and we got one guy into a fairly serious hyperthermia situation after using a cold mountain lake to float materials for trail bridges a shorter distance than hiking them around the lake. Great idea, but several us of took too many trips. We had a sleeping bag with us in a day kit, but it lost most of its thermal capacity when it got wet from the guys soaked clothes (dumb us: take the wet clothes off first!...) One of these emergency blankets and with room for a second person would have been an easier way to get him back to normal, and taken a lot less space.

From a price point of view, you can find single blankets for $5 to $20 bucks, depending on sale prices, quality and so forth. Thus, this double-sized version is priced at essentially no difference in cost and works for two. Construction is great. Four stars only because it's not a super premium version (which of course would cost more.) (EDITED to five stars, responding to a comment -- I agree.) These are designed for emergencies, so you are not buying this for multiple uses. This version seems to be at the right price point.

Hope this is helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Grizzly Gear Emergency Survival Mylar Thermal 2 Person Sleeping Bag - Accommodates 2 Adults - 64" X 87"

CUZINA HexPro Pickleball Racquetball Glove So far so good with this CUZINA HexPro Pickleball Racquetball Glove. This will be mine, but my wife likes it so much she would like to get one as well.

The size is spot on for me and very comfortable. I was actually a little surprised by how thick it is - and thrilled by how comfortable it feels on. I think the only question I have here is, will it be too hot during play? Yet I also feel like it'll help with keeping sweat from loosening my grip and making the hand feel raw because of it.

As of this writing I have not been able to use it while playing (time available to play vs. rain and extreme heat and humidity has kept us off the court), so I'll update if things do not turn out as expected. However, my wife and I feel the chance of that happening is pretty slim. We have both had it on - fits and feels great. We have both swung the paddle with it - a few different paddles - and it has a great grip. So the only thing we can't test yet (ironically) is how it will feel while playing - does it get too hot and become uncomfortable - we are predicting, no. But will update if needed.

Overall we both think this is going to be a great glove for us and are planning to get her one. In the mean time, we love the look, love the feel, and can't wait to be able to get back on the court and getting to use it!
